relationships.name: Tasha Jenkins
relationships.notes: Tasha is 42, works part-time as a receptionist, lives with Esther and is her only local informal support. Before the acute presentation Esther did not require care from her.

background.summary: Lives with her daughter Tasha in a rented two-bedroom terraced house.
background.details: The property has stairs and no downstairs toilet or bathroom.

background.summary: Widowed and experienced a depressive episode after her husband's death.
background.details: Previously took antidepressants for two years.

background.summary: There is a significant family history of cardiovascular and metabolic disease.
background.details: Her mother died from a stroke aged 85; a sister died from heart disease aged 65; her father had high cholesterol and diabetes.

background.summary: Smokes approximately ten cigarettes daily and has smoked since age 18.
background.details: She would like to stop but is reluctant to add smoking-cessation medication to her existing medicines.

background.summary: Usually eats simple or ready-prepared meals and undertakes little regular exercise.
background.details: Walks for about 30 minutes once or twice a month and drinks alcohol occasionally.

background.summary: Fully independent before the acute presentation.
background.details: Managed personal care, dressing, mobility and domestic tasks without a package of care, equipment, home adaptations or previous adult-social-care involvement.

problems.details: Occurred after bereavement and was treated with antidepressants for two years.
Increasing low mood over several months before the acute presentation, not previously disclosed. No hopelessness, self-harm thoughts, hallucinations or delusions were reported.

allergies.details: Patient-reported reaction in the source profile.

baselineMedications.details: Exact medicine requires reconciliation with the GP or pharmacy record.
Morning adherence is good, but evening doses are often forgotten; approximately three evening doses were missed in the week before the acute presentation.
Dose not recalled and not taken for approximately two months; interaction risk with apixaban should be reviewed before use.

entries.summary: Hypertension diagnosed approximately ten years ago.
entries.outcome: Hypertension diagnosed; a recent home reading was approximately 160/90 mmHg.

entries.summary: Atrial fibrillation diagnosed approximately two years ago.
entries.outcome: Atrial fibrillation diagnosed and anticoagulation with apixaban started.

entries.summary: Recent home blood pressure was approximately 160/90 mmHg.
Depressive episode following her husband's death, subsequently resolved.
entries.outcome: Depressive episode identified after bereavement and treated with antidepressants for two years.

entries.summary: Two-year course of antidepressant treatment following bereavement.
entries.reasonEnded: Course completed; depressive episode recorded as resolved.

catalogue.synopsis: An older adult with hypertension and atrial fibrillation, living with and supported by her daughter, suitable for acute stroke and interprofessional learning.
